q1_issues.issue: the restrictive relative clause "in which one always cheats" restricts the predicate nominal "game", but the parse detaches it into a free-standing generic whose oblique points at love, so nothing records what kind of game love is said to be.
the rule ranges over (Member $x person) at strength 1.0, asserting of every person that they always cheat, whereas the impersonal "one" is restricted to whoever is playing that game.

q2_gaps: a restrictive relative clause modifying the PREDICATE NOMINAL of a kind-level copular clause ("X is a N in which ...") -- no rule says whether to fuse a restricted subkind, seal the clause, or split it off as an independent generic
the impersonal generic pronoun "one" ("one always cheats") -- the pronoun rules cover only referential he/she/it/they with or without an antecedent, not the generic-human "one"
notes: The "always" handling is correct on both channels (rule strength 1.0 plus the QuantifierPhrase companion in the prescribed <kind> <verb-lemma> "<word>" shape), and (Inheritance love game) at 0.9 matches the empirical dial.
